samples.summary: `headingLevel` is interpolated into DOCX XML unescaped, and the clipboard deserializer accepts arbitrary block fields without validation
samples.evidence: `buildParagraphPropertiesXml` builds `<w:pStyle w:val="Heading${headingLevel}"/>` by raw string interpolation (packages/docs/src/export/docx-style-map.ts:96). Every persisted path coerces the field with `Number(...)` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:438, packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:409), so CRDT-borne values are safe. The one uncoerced entry point is `deserializeClipboard` (packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:38-49), which only checks `version === 1` and `Array.isArray(payload.blocks)` and then casts to `Block[]`; those blocks are inserted verbatim by packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:1206. An attacker who gets a victim to paste a crafted `application/x-waffledocs` payload containing `{type:'heading', headingLevel:'1"/><w:pStyle w:val="'}` would have that string flow into the exported .docx XML in the same session, breaking out of the attribute. Impact is limited to corrupting/injecting markup in a document the victim exports (no code execution in the app), and the weakness is pre-existing rather than introduced here — this change only makes the attribute survive longer on list-items, which does not widen the sink. Reported for completeness; fix is to validate/clamp `headingLevel` on clipboard ingest or escape it at the XML sink.
searchedFor: Grep deserializeClipboard|deserializeBlocks call sites in packages/**/src/**/*.ts
